correctness.rationale: For b in (0,1/2), min right >= b and max left <= 1-b fail with probability at most 2 n b^2. Each of the two spanning-interval types occurs independently for each interval with exact probability b; a union bound gives another 2 exp(-nb). The selected intervals overlap and together cover the entire extreme transversal segment, so they dominate. The case when one interval satisfies both types is handled by universal adjacency. Substitution b=2 log(n)/n is admissible for n>=9. The diameter<=2/universal equivalence is proved using the earliest finishing and latest starting intervals. The exact complete-graph mass follows from n! cross-cut pairings among (2n-1)!! total. The known exact universal probability 2/3 is independently attributed to Justicz-Scheinerman-Winkler (1990) and reaffirmed by Diaconis-Holmes-Janson (2012). The delivered program exhausts 146598 rank-pairings through seven intervals. No finite test substitutes for the all-n proof.

value.rationale: Ordinary domination, connected domination, total domination and graph diameter are canonical global invariants. A bounded two-adjacent-vertex total dominating set with quantitative error is a non-obvious global coverage phenomenon in this random interval model, especially in contrast with diverging independent packing. It gives the full asymptotic 2/3-versus-1/3 diameter split, not just the already known universal-vertex mass. The result is distribution-free and self-contained aside from the explicitly attributed classical 2/3 lemma; no downstream theorem is needed for its standalone mathematical value.
